claim_1.claim: Affymetrix arrays analysis of PBMCs from 21 healthy, YFV seronegative volunteers at 4 h and Days 1, 2, 3, 5, 7, 14, 28, 84 and 168 post-vaccination showed that YF-17D vaccination induced broad transcriptional changes compared to baseline (Day 0).

sources.quote: YF-17D vaccination induced broad transcriptional changes, as evidenced by the finding that 1001 significantly differentially expressed genes (DEGs) were modulated at least one time-point postvaccination as compared to their prevaccination levels (Supplemental Table 1).

claim_2.claim: Affymetrix arrays analysis of PBMCs from 21 healthy, YFV seronegative volunteers at 4 h and Days 1, 2, 3, 5, 7, 14, 28, 84 and 168 post-vaccination showed that the number of differentially expressed genes peaked at Days 2 and 5 compared to Hour 4, Day 1, Day 3, Day 7, Day 14, and Day 28.

sources.quote: The number of DEGs changes peaked at Days 2 and 5, and then returned to baseline levels at Day 28 (Figure 1A).

Figure 1. Kinetics of the peripheral blood mononuclear cell transcriptomic response to the YF-17D vaccine. (A) Upper panel: Number of differentially expressed genes (DEGs) (threshold fold change > 1.5 and Benjamini-Hochberg adjusted false discovery rate < 0.01) in peripheral blood mononuclear cells at Hour 4, Day 1, Day 2, Day 3, Day 5, Day 7, Day 14, and Day 28 post YF-17D vaccination compared with their baseline (prevaccination) levels as calculated by the empirical Bayes test.

claim_3.claim: Affymetrix arrays analysis of PBMCs from 21 healthy, YFV seronegative volunteers at 4 h and Days 1, 2, 3, 5, 7, 14, 28, 84 and 168 post-vaccination showed that the number of differentially expressed genes returned to baseline by Day 28 compared to the earlier post-vaccination timepoints.

sources.quote: The number of DEGs changes peaked at Days 2 and 5, and then returned to baseline levels at Day 28 (Figure 1A).

Figure 1. Kinetics of the peripheral blood mononuclear cell transcriptomic response to the YF-17D vaccine. (A) Upper panel: Number of differentially expressed genes (DEGs) (threshold fold change > 1.5 and Benjamini-Hochberg adjusted false discovery rate < 0.01) in peripheral blood mononuclear cells at Hour 4, Day 1, Day 2, Day 3, Day 5, Day 7, Day 14, and Day 28 post YF-17D vaccination compared with their baseline (prevaccination) levels as calculated by the empirical Bayes test.

claim_4.claim: Affymetrix arrays analysis of PBMCs from 21 healthy, YFV seronegative volunteers at 4 h and Days 1, 2, 3, 5, 7, 14, 28, 84 and 168 post-vaccination showed that JUP, STAT1, and EIF2AK2 expression peaked on Days 5 and 7 compared to Hour 4, Day 1, Day 2, Day 3, Day 14, and Day 28.

sources.quote: Of these, JUP, STAT1, and EIF2AK2 reached their peak expression levels on Days 5 and 7, and mitosis-related (e.g. CCNA2, CCNB1, and TOP2A) and cell cycle-related (e.g. CDK1 and CDC6) genes were upregulated at Day 14 after vaccination.

claim_5.claim: Affymetrix arrays analysis of PBMCs from 21 healthy, YFV seronegative volunteers at 4 h and Days 1, 2, 3, 5, 7, 14, 28, 84 and 168 post-vaccination showed that mitosis-related genes CCNA2, CCNB1, and TOP2A and cell cycle-related genes CDK1 and CDC6 were upregulated at Day 14 compared to baseline (Day 0).

sources.quote: Of these, JUP, STAT1, and EIF2AK2 reached their peak expression levels on Days 5 and 7, and mitosis-related (e.g. CCNA2, CCNB1, and TOP2A) and cell cycle-related (e.g. CDK1 and CDC6) genes were upregulated at Day 14 after vaccination.

claim_6.claim: Affymetrix arrays analysis of PBMCs from 21 healthy, YFV seronegative volunteers at 4 h and Days 1, 2, 3, 5, 7, 14, 28, 84 and 168 post-vaccination showed that transcription factors EEF1A1, JUN, NFKBIA, REL, FOS, JUND, and TP53, cell cycle regulators CDC42 and CDKN1A, chemokine and cytokine genes CXCR4, TNFAIP3, and TRAF6, and cell matrix genes MMP9 and THBS1 were upregulated at Day 28 compared to baseline (Day 0).

sources.quote: Moreover, at Day 28, transcription factors (e.g. EEF1A1, JUN, NFKBIA, REL, FOS, JUND, and TP53), cell cycle regulators (CDC42 and CDKN1A), chemokine and cytokines (CXCR4, TNFAIP3, TRAF6), and cell matrix (MMP9, THBS1) genes were upregulated.

claim_7.claim: Affymetrix arrays analysis of PBMCs from 21 healthy, YFV seronegative volunteers at 4 h and Days 1, 2, 3, 5, 7, 14, 28, 84 and 168 post-vaccination, using Ingenuity Pathway Analysis, showed that the pattern recognition receptor, TNF receptor-mediated, TREM-1, and IL-6/IL-1 pathways were inhibited over two weeks post-vaccination compared to baseline (Day 0).

sources.quote: The top inhibited pathways, defined by drastic gene downregulation sustained over two weeks postvaccination, included the pattern recognition receptor (PRR), TNF receptor-mediated, TREM-1, and IL-6/IL-1 pathways.

claim_8.claim: Affymetrix arrays analysis of PBMCs from 21 healthy, YFV seronegative volunteers at 4 h and Days 1, 2, 3, 5, 7, 14, 28, 84 and 168 post-vaccination, using Ingenuity Pathway Analysis, showed that the PPAR-mediated pathway and the LXR/RXR activation pathway reached maximal activation at 4 h compared to Day 1, Day 2, Day 3, Day 5, Day 7, Day 14, and Day 28.

sources.quote: Meanwhile, the peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor (PPAR)-mediated pathway, which plays essential roles in the regulation of cellular differentiation, development, and metabolism (carbohydrate, lipid, protein) (37, 38), and the LXR/RXR activation pathway were activated to their maximum extent at 4 h; this activation persisted over the entire time course.

claim_9.claim: Affymetrix arrays analysis of PBMCs from 21 healthy, YFV seronegative volunteers at 4 h and Days 1, 2, 3, 5, 7, 14, 28, 84 and 168 post-vaccination, using Ingenuity Pathway Analysis, showed that activation of the PPAR-mediated pathway and the LXR/RXR activation pathway persisted over the entire time course compared to baseline (Day 0).

sources.quote: Meanwhile, the peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor (PPAR)-mediated pathway, which plays essential roles in the regulation of cellular differentiation, development, and metabolism (carbohydrate, lipid, protein) (37, 38), and the LXR/RXR activation pathway were activated to their maximum extent at 4 h; this activation persisted over the entire time course.

claim_10.claim: Affymetrix arrays analysis of PBMCs from 21 healthy, YFV seronegative volunteers at 4 h and Days 1, 2, 3, 5, 7, 14, 28, 84 and 168 post-vaccination, using Ingenuity Pathway Analysis, showed that cytosolic pattern recognition receptors, RIG-1 like receptors, and PI3K/AKT signaling pathways were activated from Day 1 to Day 7 compared to baseline (Day 0).

sources.quote: Specifically, cytosolic pattern recognition receptors, RIG-1 like receptors, and PI3K/AKT signaling pathways were activated from Day 1 to Day 7 (Figure 2); these sensors lead to downstream activation of interferon-regulatory factor (IRF) transcription factors and subsequent induction of antiviral cascades (40).

Figure 2. Ingenuity Pathway Analysis (IPA) of biological pathways significantly activated or inhibited in peripheral blood mononuclear cells at different time-points post YF-17D vaccination. Transcriptomic data from peripheral blood mononuclear cells harvested at baseline (prevaccination), Hour 4, Day 1, Day 2, Day 3, Day 5, Day 7, Day 14, and Day 28 post YF-17D vaccination were analyzed using IPA software to identify canonical biological pathways that were significantly activated or inhibited in PBMCs in response to YF-17D vaccination compared to their baseline (prevaccination) status.

claim_11.claim: Affymetrix arrays analysis of PBMCs from 21 healthy, YFV seronegative volunteers at 4 h and Days 1, 2, 3, 5, 7, 14, 28, 84 and 168 post-vaccination, using Ingenuity Pathway Analysis, showed that the interferon signaling pathway was highly activated on Days 2, 5, and 7 compared to baseline (Day 0).

sources.quote: Consistent with the expression of individual genes involved in interferon signaling (Figure 1), this pathway was highly activated on Days 2, 5, and 7.

claim_12.claim: Affymetrix arrays analysis of PBMCs from 21 healthy, YFV seronegative volunteers at 4 h and Days 1, 2, 3, 5, 7, 14, 28, 84 and 168 post-vaccination, using Ingenuity Pathway Analysis, showed that activation of the interferon signaling pathway trended back to baseline by Day 14 compared to Days 2, 5, and 7.

sources.quote: By Day 14, the activation of the interferon pathway trended to the baseline level and cell cycle-related pathways were instead activated or inhibited, suggesting that by this point the immune system had recovered from the perturbation.

claim_13.claim: Affymetrix arrays analysis of PBMCs from 21 healthy, YFV seronegative volunteers at 4 h and Days 1, 2, 3, 5, 7, 14, 28, 84 and 168 post-vaccination, using Ingenuity Pathway Analysis, showed that the p38/ERK MAPK pathway was transiently inhibited at 4 h (day 0) and then activated through Days 1 and 2 before becoming inhibited again compared to baseline (Day 0).

sources.quote: The p38/ERK MAPK pathway was transiently inhibited at 4 h postvaccination and then activated through Days 1 and 2 postvaccination, after which it was again inhibited.

claim_14.claim: Affymetrix arrays analysis of PBMCs from 21 healthy, YFV seronegative volunteers at 4 h and Days 1, 2, 3, 5, 7, 14, 28, 84 and 168 post-vaccination, using Ingenuity Pathway Analysis, showed that Protein Kinase A signaling pathways were activated from 4 h through Day 2 and then became inhibited compared to baseline (Day 0).

sources.quote: In contrast, Protein Kinase A signaling pathways exhibited sustained activation from 4 h through to Day 2, after which they were similarly inhibited.

claim_15.claim: Affymetrix arrays analysis of PBMCs from 21 healthy, YFV seronegative volunteers at 4 h and Days 1, 2, 3, 5, 7, 14, 28, 84 and 168 post-vaccination, using Blood Transcription Module analysis, showed that module responses peaked at Day 5 compared to Hour 4, Day 1, Day 2, Day 3, Day 7, Day 14, and Day 28.

sources.quote: This analysis reflected similar patterns to those observed at the gene level. For example, the module responses peaked at Day 5 (15 upregulated modules), waned by Day 7 (6 upregulated modules), and returned to the baseline level by Day 28 (Figure 3).

Figure 3. Blood Transcription Module (BTM) analysis of functional gene modules significantly differentially expressed in peripheral blood mononuclear cells in response to YF-17D vaccination. Innate immune responses in transcriptomic data from peripheral blood mononuclear cells harvested at baseline (prevaccination), Hour 4, Day 1, Day 2, Day 3, Day 5, Day 7, Day 14, and Day 28 post YF-17D vaccination were identified by BTM analysis.

claim_16.claim: Affymetrix arrays analysis of PBMCs from 21 healthy, YFV seronegative volunteers at 4 h and Days 1, 2, 3, 5, 7, 14, 28, 84 and 168 post-vaccination, using Blood Transcription Module analysis, showed that module responses waned by Day 7 compared to Day 5.

sources.quote: This analysis reflected similar patterns to those observed at the gene level. For example, the module responses peaked at Day 5 (15 upregulated modules), waned by Day 7 (6 upregulated modules), and returned to the baseline level by Day 28 (Figure 3).

claim_18.claim: Affymetrix arrays analysis of PBMCs from 21 healthy, YFV seronegative volunteers at 4 h and Days 1, 2, 3, 5, 7, 14, 28, 84 and 168 post-vaccination, using Blood Transcription Module analysis, showed that innate immune response modules including antiviral type I interferon signature, activated dendritic cells, RIG-1 like receptor signaling, chemokines, complement activation, IRF2-targeting network, and FOSL were induced on Days 2, 5, and 7 compared to baseline (Day 0).

sources.quote: Modules induced by YF-17D vaccination were associated with the innate immune response (e.g. antiviral type I interferon signature, activated dendritic cells, RIG-1 like receptor signaling, chemokines, complement activation, IRF2-targeting network, and FOSL) at Days 2, 5 and 7.

claim_19.claim: Affymetrix arrays analysis of PBMCs from 21 healthy, YFV seronegative volunteers at 4 h and Days 1, 2, 3, 5, 7, 14, 28, 84 and 168 post-vaccination, using Blood Transcription Module analysis, showed that PLK1 signaling and B cell related modules including memory B cell surface signature, plasma cell, and immunoglobulin were enriched at Day 14 compared to baseline (Day 0).

sources.quote: Concomitantly, the cell division/cycle progression relative critical regulator PLK1 signaling and B cell related modules (e.g. memory B cell surface signature, plasma cell and immunoglobulin) were enriched at Day 14, indicating enhanced humoral immunological responses.

claim_20.claim: Flow cytometry analysis of PBMCs from 21 healthy, YFV seronegative volunteers at Day 0, Day 7, Day 14, Day 28, and Day 86 post-vaccination showed that the percentage of monocytes in PBMCs decreased at Day 14 compared to baseline (Day 0).

sources.quote: Regarding innate immune cells, compared to baseline levels at 0 h, the percentage of monocytes in PBMCs decreased significantly at Day 14 (p = 0.01) after a negligible change at Day 7, and later increased at Day 86 (p = 0.095) (Figure 4A).

Figure 4. Kinetics of monocyte, dendritic cell, natural killer (NK) phenotype, and NK functional responses to YF-17D vaccination. Percentages of (A) monocytes, (B, C) dendritic cells, and (D to F) NK cells out of total peripheral blood mononuclear cells harvested at baseline (prevaccination, Day 0) and then again at Days 7, 14, 28, and 86 post YF-17D vaccination. Immunophenotyping was performed by flow cytometry.

sources.quote: Regarding innate immune cells, compared to baseline levels at 0 h, the percentage of monocytes in PBMCs decreased significantly at Day 14 (p = 0.01) after a negligible change at Day 7, and later increased at Day 86 (p = 0.095) (Figure 4A).

sources.quote: The percentage of DCs fluctuated postvaccination, with the percentages of CD11c+ (Figure 4B) and CD123+ (Figure 4C) cells significantly increased at Day 86 vs. 0 h, and the percentage of plasmacytoid DCs (CD123+) also significantly increased at Days 7 and 28 vs. 0 h.

sources.quote: Generally, the percentage of NK cells decreased after vaccination, with the same trend for both activated (NKp46) (Figure 4F) and inhibitory (NKG2A) (Figure 4E) markers.

claim_25.claim: Flow cytometry analysis of PBMCs from 21 healthy, YFV seronegative volunteers at Day 0, Day 7, Day 14, Day 28, and Day 86 post-vaccination showed that NK-mediated cytotoxicity measured by antibody-dependent cell-mediated cytotoxicity activity and TNF-α, IFN-γ, and CD107a secretion increased at Day 7 compared to baseline (Day 0).

sources.quote: NK-mediated cytotoxicity, as assessed by ADCC activity or secretion of the cytokines TNF-α, IFN-γ, and CD107a, increased significantly at Day 7 and dropped to baseline levels at and after Day 14 (Figure 4 G-I).

Figure 4. Kinetics of monocyte, dendritic cell, natural killer (NK) phenotype, and NK functional responses to YF-17D vaccination. (G to I) Percentages of NK cells displaying antibody-dependent cell-mediated cytotoxicity.

sources.quote: NK-mediated cytotoxicity, as assessed by ADCC activity or secretion of the cytokines TNF-α, IFN-γ, and CD107a, increased significantly at Day 7 and dropped to baseline levels at and after Day 14 (Figure 4 G-I).

claim_27.claim: Flow cytometry analysis of PBMCs from 21 healthy, YFV seronegative volunteers at Day 0, Day 7, Day 14, Day 28, and Day 86 post-vaccination showed that B cell populations increased at Day 14 and remained elevated through Day 86 compared to baseline (Day 0).

sources.quote: Flow cytometry staining of PBMCs revealed that B cell populations increased at Day 14 vs. Day 0 (p = 0.021) and persisted at high levels for 3 months (p = 0.029 and 0.02 at Day 28 and Day 86, respectively), as shown in Figure 5.

Figure 5. Percentages of B cell and T cell subsets and changes in T cell function over time in response to YF-17D vaccination. Peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) were harvested at Day 0 (prevaccination) and then again at Day 7, Day 14, Day 28, and Day 86 post YF-17D vaccination. PBMCs were stained with cocktails of antibodies to identify B cell subsets (A to E) and T cell subsets (F to I) and analyzed by flow cytometry.

claim_28.claim: Flow cytometry analysis of PBMCs from 21 healthy, YFV seronegative volunteers at Day 0, Day 7, Day 14, Day 28, and Day 86 post-vaccination showed that the mature B cell population (IgD+ IgM+) increased after Day 7 and remained elevated until Day 86 compared to baseline (Day 0).

sources.quote: Similar to the overall B cell populations, the mature B cell population (IgD+ IgM+) increased after Day 7 (p < 0.001) and remained at a high level until Day 86 (p < 0.001) (Figure 5 B).

sources.quote: The IgM-only memory B cells (IgD- IgM+ CD27+) showed a significant boost from Day 28 to Day 86 (Figure 5 C).

sources.quote: The percentage of class-switched memory B cells (IgD- IgM- CD27+) (shown in Figure 5 D) slightly decreased at Day 7 but recovered by Day 86.

claim_31.claim: Flow cytometry analysis of PBMCs from 21 healthy, YFV seronegative volunteers at Day 0, Day 7, Day 14, Day 28, and Day 86 post-vaccination showed that the percentages of CD4+ and CD8+ T cells expressing CD28 and Ki67 decreased at Day 7 compared to baseline (Day 0).

sources.quote: The percentages of CD4+ and CD8+ T cells expressing CD28 and Ki67 decreased (p < 0.001, p = 0.03, p < 0.001, p = 0.001, respectively) at Day 7 vs. Day 0 (shown in Figure 5 E-H), implying that T cell proliferation was unexpectedly suppressed by vaccination.

claim_32.claim: Flow cytometry analysis of PBMCs from 21 healthy, YFV seronegative volunteers at Day 0, Day 7, Day 14, Day 28, and Day 86 post-vaccination after stimulation with YFV NS1 and Env peptide pools showed that YFV-specific IL-2 secretion by CD4+ cells increased at Day 28 and Day 86 compared to baseline (Day 0).

sources.quote: This analysis revealed that secretion of YFV-specific IL-2 by CD4+ cells (as shown in Figure 5 I, J) increased at Day 28 and Day 86 post vaccination after stimulation with NS1 and Env antigens, respectively (p = 0.07 and p = 0.038).
Alternatively, PBMCs were stimulated with YFV peptide pools and subjected to intracellular cytokine staining to measure T cell function (I and J).

claim_33.claim: Immunofluorescence assay analysis of serum from 21 healthy volunteers at baseline showed that 6 of 21 subjects were seropositive to at least one of West Nile virus or Japanese encephalitis virus compared to the remaining participants who were seronegative.

sources.quote: We found that six out of the 21 subjects were seropositive to at least one of the flaviviruses tested (Supplemental Figure 3).

claim_34.claim: Affymetrix arrays analysis of PBMCs from WNV/JEV-seropositive and WNV/JEV-seronegative participants showed no variation in gene profiles by WNV/JEV seropositivity compared between the two baseline serostatus groups.

sources.quote: However, participants’ gene profiles did not seem to vary according to WNV/JEV seropositivity (data not shown).

claim_35.claim: Flow cytometry analysis of PBMCs from WNV/JEV-seronegative and WNV/JEV-seropositive participants at Days 14, 28, and 86 post-vaccination showed that the percentage of myeloid dendritic cells was higher in WNV/JEV-seronegative participants compared to WNV/JEV-seropositive participants.

sources.quote: The percentage of myeloid dendritic cells was higher in WNV/JEV-seronegative participants from Day 14 through Day 86 post vaccination compared to WNV/JEV-seropositive participants (Figure 6A).

Figure 6. Cellular immunological responses in baseline flavivirus-seropositive vs. flavivirus-naïve participants. Serum samples taken at baseline were screened by immunofluorescence assay to identify samples with antibodies reactive against West Nile virus and/or Japanese encephalitis virus. Of the 21 participants, 6 showed a pre-existing flavivirus seropositivity. PBMCs were analyzed by flow cytometry immunophenotyping of DCs (A) and B cells (C), NK cells (B) and T cell functional analyses (D) followed by intracellular cytokine staining.

sources.quote: Interestingly, WNV/JEV-seropositive volunteers showed higher levels of NK activity than WNV/JEV-seronegative participants at Days 7, 28, and 86 postvaccination (Figure 6B).

sources.quote: Interestingly, IFN-γ secretion was significantly enhanced in WNV/JEV-seropositive individuals, whereas TNF-α secretion was enhanced in WNV/JEV-seronegative participants (Figure 6D).

claim_40.claim: Affymetrix arrays analysis of PBMCs from Day 7 post-vaccination samples, using weighted gene co-expression network analysis, showed that the Turquoise module was positively associated with CD14+ macrophage cells and myeloid DC cells, the Green module was positively associated with B cells and CD28++ CD8+ T cells, the Brown module was positively associated with memory B cells (IgD- IgM+ CD27+), the Blue module was positively associated with the CD8+ T subset proliferation marker CD28, and the Yellow module was positively associated with myeloid DCs.

sources.quote: The highest MS scores observed were for the Turquoise module with CD14+ macrophage cells (MS = 0.87, p = 2e-7) and myeloid DC cells (MS = 0.69, p = 6e-4), in addition to the Green module with B cells (MS = 0.65, p = 0.001) and CD28++ CD8+ T cells (MS = 0.5, p = 0.02). In addition, the Brown module had a high score for memory B cells (IgD- IgM+ CD27+) (MS = 0.47, p = 0.03). The Blue module was significantly related to the CD8+ T subset proliferation marker CD28 (MS = 0.52, p = 0.01), whereas the Yellow module was associated with myeloid DCs (MS = 0.51, p = 0.02).
